paper.title: Learning about a New Technology: Pineapple in Ghana

paper_reference.paper_question: 加纳菠萝扩种期的农户会不会把自己的化肥用量调向信息邻里里相对 growing conditions 意外成功的实验水平，这种反应是否集中在最近才开始种菠萝的新手身上？
paper_reference.target: 八名农户在两套示范安排各 1/2 的随机政策下，下一期化肥强度相对上一季的平均变化；每人等权，变化可正可负。
paper_reference.source_location: Conley and Udry (2010) American Economic Review 100(1):35-69, DOI 10.1257/aer.100.1.35. Abstract (p. 35) for farmers aligning inputs with surprisingly successful information neighbors; Introduction (p. 37) for the signed direction rule and the novice/veteran difference; p. 43 for the construction of M and its near-zero case; p. 51 for the full signed definition of M; Table 4 note (p. 55) for the advice-question definition of information neighborhoods and the sample of 107; p. 56 for one standard deviation of M (about four) corresponding to roughly four cedis per plant, for no veteran response and for insignificant financial neighbors; Table 5 (p. 57) for M 1.05 (0.20), M x novice 1.07 (0.22) and M x veteran -0.46 (0.34); p. 58 for downward moves being as real as upward ones and for no own-plot versus neighbor-plot difference; Table 6 A (p. 59) for 1.46 (0.56) versus 1.22 (0.31); p. 60 for the maize-cassava null. Project-built scenario; the paper does not pose this question.
conditions: Two complete demonstration arrangements with known probabilities of 1/2 each.
Arrangement choice independent of the eight farmers' potential intensity changes.
Observed intensity changes correspond to the executed arrangement.
Information links are fixed before the arrangement is executed, and only the demonstration plot carries good news; other farmers' adjustments do not create new news.
The rule set applies uniformly: novices move to the demonstrated level with no move when equal, veterans never move, and the demonstrator's own change counts.
what_paper_supports: M is large and positive when a good-news experiment is much higher than the farmer's previous use, large and negative when much lower, and near zero when close (p. 51; p. 43).
For novice farmers a one-standard-deviation increase in M (about four) is associated with roughly four cedis per plant, consistent with the Table 5 A coefficient of 1.05 (p. 56; Table 5 p. 57).

Novices respond (1.07, SE 0.22) and veterans do not (-0.46, SE 0.34, not significant; different at the 3 percent level), and the text states there is no evidence of veteran response (Table 5 B p. 57; p. 56).
Strong partial correlations are driven as much by downward as by upward movement (p. 58), and own-plot good news is not significantly different from neighbor-plot good news (Table 6 A p. 59; p. 58).
what_paper_does_not_support: No claim that 1.05 is an exact multiplier: the text states about four for about four cedis, and the case rounds the coefficient to 1.

No claim that the experience normalization of M is carried into the case: the paper constructs M so that its absolute magnitude is inversely proportional to experience (p. 43), while the case keeps only the sign implication and expresses the novice/veteran difference as two separate rules.

No claim that demonstrations reproduce the paper's experiments: experiments there are farmer-chosen fertilizer levels judged against growing conditions, while the case makes the demonstration level a policy parameter set by lottery.
No claim that the good-news designation is estimated: the case stipulates that demonstration profits were above expectations, which the paper identifies through growing-condition controls.

No claim that geographic or financial neighbors carry learning: financial-neighbor coefficients are insignificant (Table 5 p. 57) and geographic neighbors enter as a growing-conditions control (p. 56).
No claim that the eight farmers stand for the paper's sample: 107 is the number of cultivators (Table 4 note p. 55) and the eight previous-use figures are project-built.
No claim of extrapolation to other crops: the paper finds no learning on the established maize-cassava mix (p. 60).

notes: Scenario adaptation; the paper does not pose this question. Network enters the target through who observes the demonstration, and the outcome is continuous and signed: each novice's change equals the demonstrated level minus previous use, so the sign of the whole target flips with where the demonstration sits. The largest departure from the paper is that the demonstration is scheduled by lottery while experiments in the paper are farmer-chosen. The mixture schema carries one fixed adjacency for all policies, so the case never changes edges across schedules; only the demonstrator moves, from farmer 1 to farmer 6.
